title: Square gauges: Boss receipt
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
A square inspection plate must fit inside each numbered sheet allowance using whole-unit edges. Neri adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement squareGaugesBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Binary search on answers. For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n log M); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with binary search on answers. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each nonnegative reading x, produce the greatest integer r with r*r <= x. Use integer comparisons rather than floating-point rounding. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.
